direction: D5: Lowering the measurement noise floor
refuted_claims:
The arithmetic is right; the mechanism behind it is mostly misattributed. On SearchQA the dominant driver of the between-text and between-session differences is the reply wrapper meeting a strict tag scorer, not items sitting on a content boundary or serving style in general. I verified this from cal1_compact.json (8,800 cells) and the v3 stage-1 SearchQA training cells (train/screen/confirm units only), read on the new machine.

1. Claim: "the noise level is a property of the Skill text... texts that pin the answer format leave half as many items on the decision boundary; cand and control:3 push more items onto it".
   - Found: replies wrapped as {"answer": ...} score 0 in every arm (0 passes out of 364). In 414 of 424 JSON replies, the identical answer string also appears inside an <answer> tag on the same item, and in 324 of those 414 the tagged version passed. So the zero is a format artifact.
   - Restricted to pairs where both runs are tagged, run-to-run disagreement is 0.039-0.059 for every text except cand (0.080). Scaffold A/B 0.059/0.054, ids-full 0.049, seed-only 0.042, control:3 0.049.
   - Pairs involving an untagged or JSON reply account for 56-58% of the scaffold's disagreeing pairs and 75-81% of those for cand, control:3 and seed-rule3.

2. Claim: "Irrelevant texts are not null. control:3 costs -10.1 points... Deterministic serving would not remove this" (cand about -2.3).
   - Method: I rescored only the JSON replies with the verdict their identical answer string received inside a tag on the same item.
   - control:3: -0.100 → -0.005 (t -5.15 → -0.31).
   - cand (the v3 learned rule s1-r1): -0.0275 → +0.064 (t -1.19 → +3.35), and its noise 0.161 → 0.093.
   - seed-rule3: -0.031 → +0.030.
   - The "placebo harm" is a JSON side effect (control:3 emits 15.8% JSON). The learned rule's content effect looks positive but is masked by its 14.7% JSON rate. This rescoring is post hoc and heuristic.

3. Claim R1: "For empty-scaffold experiments, add a fixed answer-format line" (halves the noise, immune to drift).
   - seed-rule (scaffold + the seed's "minimal entity" answer-form sentence) and seed-rule3 (+ the seed's other answer-form sentences) are exactly such lines, and cal-1 already measured them.
   - Their noise is 0.097 and 0.123, against 0.105 for the scaffold.
   - Untagged replies rise to 21% and 25%, and JSON to 2.6% and 9.5%. Content-form lines make wrapper compliance worse, so the proposed fix is untested and its nearest tested analogues contradict it.

4. Claim: the task card takes the noise from 0.105 to about 0.05, "so the fixed-panel item count halves".
   - The same task-card text had noise 0.090 (SE 0.020) in the v3 I-ds s1 training rollout and 0.058 in the s1 screen. The scaffold had 0.035 in its terse session. T7 itself uses 0.090 for SearchQA.
   - Content-level (tag-tag) noise is the same for both texts in cal-1 (0.052 vs 0.049) and ranges 0.026-0.086 across sessions for both.
   - The "halving" is one session's wrapper component, not a stable property of the task card.

5. Claim: "in a terse session the empty scaffold scores about 5.7 points higher" (drift as a general verdict bias).
   - Both significant comparisons reuse the same single terse session (E-ds s1 train).
   - The three other terse scaffold sessions (s2, s3 and s4 screens, 29 overlapping items) give -3.45, 0.0 and -1.72 points. The report merges them with task-card rows as "-0.034 to +0.052, all n.s.", which hides this.
   - On the 135 items whose scaffold replies were tagged in both sessions, terse minus verbose is +0.0037 [-0.034, +0.042] (11 up / 8 down). The whole effect sits on the 65 items with any untagged or JSON reply: +0.169, 33/7.
   - The train-minus-screen drop behaves the same way: +0.0015 on the 168 always-tagged items.
   - Task-card "immunity" rests on one 200-item terse-vs-verbose comparison, 0.000 ± 0.031. The second cited comparison (+0.001) is verbose against verbose (7.7% vs 5.8% bare replies).

6. Claim: "a roughly constant ~3% per-token hazard is what batch variance predicts... our measurements fit".
   - The report shows only the table bucketed by the longer reply. The explorer's own noise2 table, bucketed by the shorter reply, gives 0.19-0.20 per token for 1-8-token replies and 0.09-0.11 for 9-16.
   - 34.6% of differing parent pairs differ at the first character (a bare answer against a reasoning preamble). Much of the divergence is a style or format switch, which batch-invariant kernels alone would not remove.

7. Cost basis of "about 1,594 tokens per call":
   - cal-1 attempt-1's ledger settled 24.87M tokens for 7,205 cells, about 3,450 per cell (the registration notes it was twice the estimate). Attempt-2 settled at 1,622 per cell.
   - The panel-cost estimates can therefore be about 2× low in a loaded session.

8. Claim: "no design using only the training pool can see effects below about 7-12 points" on OfficeQA, SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld.
   - That range holds for generalization claims at 2-4 runs.
   - With the explorer's own formula and many runs, the generalization floor is 6.1 (OfficeQA), 4.8 (SpreadsheetBench) and 6.9 (ALFWorld) points.
   - For fixed-panel gates at 8 runs it is about 3.5-4.9 points.

9. Minor: "a per-request seed would make T1 repeats near-identical; 2/48 rules that out". On a batch-variant server a seed that is honoured would only reach T0 level (9/48). The item-level test (0 more / 5 fewer identical pairs vs T0) gives p = 0.06. The conclusion stands on seed="not-an-integer" returning 200.

10. Scope: "never vote anywhere in the evaluation layer" is shown only for pass-rate estimation from solver verdicts. It says nothing about categorical judge labels (v4's 3-vote reason-then-label roles).
confirmed_claims:
Recomputed from the data:
- cal-1 has 8,800 cells: 6,008 pass, 2,777 fail, 15 unknown; run indices 0-3.
- Per-arm noise: parent:A 0.1175, parent:B 0.1025, pooled 0.105, ids-full 0.049, seed-only 0.054, cand 0.161, control:3 0.161. Mixed items: 41/200 and 18/200.
- parent:A − parent:B: −0.0075 [−0.027, +0.012], 16 up / 20 down / 164 tie. One-run diagonals: −12, +7, +2, −3. The SD of all 16 one-run pairings is 5.9 items, while the 2-run pairings match the analytic value.
- The analytic SD formula gives 4.59 / 3.25 / 2.29 items at 1 / 2 / 4 runs.
- Majority-of-3 exact unbiased variance ratio: 0.759. A plug-in on all 8 runs gives 0.776, so the earlier draft's 0.507 was not just plug-in bias on this data (minor).
- Item heterogeneity: ids-full 0.076, cand 0.072, control:1 0.014, control:3 0.041.
- Per-session style shares and the 200-item paired results: +0.0575 [0.019, 0.096] 44/15; +0.0563; task card 0.000.
- T6a and T7 arithmetic, including the 7.849 and 6.183 factors. Pool sizes 600 / 74 / 283 / 120 / 57 are the train+val pools that coevo5/data.py merges into training, so they are not a fixed validation set.

Route (from the pilot logs):
- seed, top_k, n and logprobs are dropped; seed="not-an-integer" returns 200. The pilot builds the HTTP body itself, so the gateway drops them, not the client.
- top_p, temperature and max_tokens return 400 with vLLM-verbatim messages. No system_fingerprint.
- P1 identical pairs out of 48: 9 / 2 / 2 / 0 / 12. P2 identical pairs 16/72 vs 19/72; verdict differs 27/72 vs 23/72.

Literature, all checked at source:
- Thinking Machines: Qwen3-235B, 80 unique completions out of 1,000, the most common 78 times, first divergence at token 103, load-dependent batch size, no client-side remedy. The 26 / 55 / 42-second timings are for Qwen3-8B.
- vLLM: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, beta; validated DeepSeek-V3, V3-0324, R1 and V3.1; no V4.
- SGLang: --enable-deterministic-inference, 34.35% average slowdown, dense models only, DeepSeek-V3 "planned".
- Miller Eq. (9) is exactly as stated.
- Atil et al.: 15% / 70%. Yuan et al.: 9% / 9,000 tokens, LayerCast.
- DeepSeek API: no seed, top_k or n; top_p ignored in non-thinking mode; system_fingerprint present.

Recommendations that stand: interleave every compared arm in one shuffled pool; average runs rather than vote when estimating pass rates; size panels and state the MDE; drop seed/top_k/top_p/concurrency tuning; report both SE components. OfficeQA and LiveMath noise is content noise (tag-tag noise equals overall noise: 0.082-0.085 and 0.128-0.162), so those figures stand.
missing:
1. The format channel is the cheapest lever, and it is not request parameters.
   - On SearchQA, JSON replies are always scored wrong, and untagged prose is mostly scored wrong through the scorer's fallback.
   - Scoring content and format compliance separately in the training-side gates (a deterministic wrapper parse, or one format-repair re-ask; format still counted under C3; the official metric kept for test) would roughly:
     - halve the scaffold's noise (0.106 → about 0.052);
     - cut the candidate's (0.161 → about 0.09);
     - remove the session-drift bias (always-tagged items: +0.4 points);
     - remove the spurious placebo effect.
   - A tag-pinning line, as opposed to a content-form line, needs a pilot of about 400 calls.

2. Re-reading v3 and cal-1 rule verdicts under content scoring. The cand rule rescores to +6.4 points (t 3.35), which bears on the "zero rules accepted" reading. This needs a pre-registered re-score, not a post hoc one.

3. v4's B13/P7 rewrites the solver framing sentence in every request. All cal-1 noise and drift numbers belong to the v3 prompt and must be re-measured at v4 step 0 (free from the training rollout).

4. MDE of the final test tables (TEST_SIZES 400 / 172 / 125 / 279 / 134, 1 run). The registered similar pairs and the paper's tables are judged on these test panels.
   - About 4-5 points on SearchQA, 6.6-7.7 on OfficeQA, 10-11 on LiveMath, 7-7.7 on SpreadsheetBench and 9-10 on ALFWorld.
   - All of these exceed the historical +3-5-point gains of learned clauses, and every registered similar pair involves OfficeQA.

5. Two hidden costs were not priced: the full re-run of the final table that R2 implies (all baselines on 5 test benchmarks, including docker SpreadsheetBench and multi-turn ALFWorld), and the 2× gap between the ledger and the usage-based cost.

6. R3's 160-call canary is largely redundant: every arm's own untagged/JSON share, logged for free, is the quantity that moves verdicts.

7. The mechanism behind the noise drop when switching to the task card was not isolated. The full seed differs from the tested lines by its tag line and its snippet guidance.

notes_cn: 总体判断：部分可信。主要数字我都复核过，没错（同一段说明文字、同一道题重跑两次，判分不一致约10%；随机种子等参数被网关丢掉）。但关键解释有误：SearchQA（检索问答）里，模型有时把答案写成JSON格式，评分器一律判错（364次全错）。“空模板噪声大”“无关对照文本扣10分”“不同时段分数差约6分”，主要都来自这个格式问题。只看答案都写进标签的题，时段差只剩0.4分，对照扣分只剩0.5分；上一轮学到的那条规则，反而从−2.8分变成+6.4分。最省钱的降噪办法，是把格式错误和答案对错分开记，而不只是换作比较基准的说明文字。按账本算，成本可能低估一倍。可行性：中等。
